request.spec:
Add an audit viewer to the screen: a filter entry, a show button and a list of lines. With the
filter blank it lists every audit line of this sheet exactly as the file holds it, newest first.
With a name in the filter it lists only the lines about that person: those carrying name=<the
name> or person=<the name>, compared as names are compared (case and surrounding spaces ignored).
The viewer reads what the file holds; it is not a second record.

agent.result_text:
The audit viewer is in place, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests: the new audit-viewer test and the three existing scenarios.

**How it works:**
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/audit?name=…` (`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/audit.GET.yml`), looks up the sheet and returns its lines. The work is done by a new read method in `Audit.java`, which reads the audit file and keeps only this sheet's lines, newest first, unchanged.
- **Name filter:** a line counts as being about a person if it carries `name=<name>` or `person=<name>`. Case and surrounding spaces in the filter are ignored, and the name has to be followed by a space or the end of the line, so filtering for "Ben" won't also match "Benny".
- **Screen:** a new panel in `src/main/frontend/features/audit/` with the filter box (`audit-filter`), the show button (`audit-show`) and one `audit-line` per line. Pressing show clears the old list first. If you press it twice quickly, only the answer to the latest press is shown.

The viewer only reads the existing audit file: it stores nothing and writes nothing to the audit trail.

The sheet is looked up the same way as in the other sheet endpoints, so asking for the audit of a sheet that was never created returns an error rather than an empty list. That never happens on screen, because a sheet is always loaded first.
